findings.problem: Lower case 'звук' where the sibling media.image_label and every other shipped locale capitalise the same label (Image/Изображение, Son, Sonido, Âm thanh). The sidecar tone field says 'bare noun, capitalised'. The lower case is, however, a reasoned choice rather than an oversight: the same value is substituted into ui.chat.audio.play_label/pause_label ('Воспроизвести {label}'), where a capital would be a mid-sentence spelling error in Russian. The two surfaces pull opposite ways and the composed aria-label is the invisible one, so the visible tile label is the weaker of the two readings.
findings.disposition: accepted, no change requested in this round
findings.replacement_if_ever_taken: {count, plural, =1 {Звук} one {Звук {position, number, ::group-off}} few {Звук {position, number, ::group-off}} many {Звук {position, number, ::group-off}} other {Звук {position, number, ::group-off}}} - and in the same change accept 'Воспроизвести Звук 2' in the accessible name, or lower case the audio play/pause template instead. Decide both surfaces together; do not flip this key alone.
findings.note: Recorded so a later wave does not silently reverse a call that reads correctly today.

findings.problem: This round-3 clause is the only full predication in a colon-count list whose siblings are labels ('Завершено: 3', 'сбоев: 1', 'остановлено: 2'), so a native reader parses 'статус неизвестен: 5' as a statement with a dangling count. It is the better of the two available readings, because it is the ONLY wording that keeps one state word across the row and the summary (item_status 'other' says 'Статус неизвестен'), which is the rule this round was asked to satisfy.
findings.disposition: accepted, no change requested in this round
findings.note: If a future wave reworks this line, change item_status 'other' and this clause in one commit; the round-2 wording 'неизвестный статус:' read better as a label but gave the same state two names.
